title: Eating for the Gym on a NZ Budget – Under $100 a Week
meta_desc: Practical NZ guide to hit protein targets on a $100 weekly budget. Cheap supermarket staples, meal plan and shopping tips for gym‑goers.
intro: Hitting your protein goals doesn’t have to break the bank. This guide shows how to fuel strength training with everyday NZ supermarket staples for under $100 a week.

sections.heading: 1. Set Your Protein Target
sections.body: Most active adults need 1.6‑2.2 g of protein per kilogram of body weight per day to support muscle repair and growth (Sports Medicine Australia). For a 75 kg lifter that’s 120‑165 g daily, or roughly 840‑1,155 g per week. Spread the intake over 3‑4 meals to maximise muscle protein synthesis and keep hunger in check.
list: Calculate your weight in kg and multiply by 1.8 g as a practical middle ground
Aim for 30‑40 g protein per main meal and 15‑20 g in snacks

sections.heading: 2. Budget‑Friendly Protein Sources
sections.body: NZ supermarkets stock a range of cheap, high‑quality protein foods. Below are the most cost‑effective options and typical Pak'nSave prices (May 2026).

sections.heading: 3. Sample 7‑Day Meal Plan (<$100)
sections.body: The plan below hits ~130 g protein per day and totals about $92 for the week. Adjust portion sizes to match your exact target and calorie needs.
list:
Day 1 – Breakfast: 80 g oats + 250 ml milk + 2 eggs (30 g protein)
Lunch: Chicken thigh stir‑fry with rice and frozen veg (35 g)
Snack: Greek yoghurt + banana (12 g)
Dinner: Lentil chilli with canned tomatoes (28 g)

Day 2 – Breakfast: Quark with berries and a drizzle of honey (22 g)
Lunch: Tuna salad (canned tuna, mixed leaf, beans) (30 g)
Snack: Handful of almonds (6 g)
Dinner: Soy mince bolognese with whole‑wheat pasta (35 g)

Day 3 – Breakfast: 3‑egg scramble with veg (27 g)
Lunch: Leftover lentil chilli (28 g)
Snack: Cottage cheese (if on sale) + apple (10 g)
Dinner: Grilled chicken thigh, sweet potato, broccoli (32 g)

Day 4 – Breakfast: Oats with whey protein (if budget allows) or extra egg (30 g)
Lunch: Tuna wrap with whole‑grain tortilla (28 g)
Snack: Greek yoghurt (10 g)
Dinner: Soy mince fried rice (35 g)

Day 5 – Breakfast: Quark parfait with muesli (22 g)
Lunch: Chicken thigh salad with beans (30 g)
Snack: Hard‑boiled eggs (12 g)
Dinner: Lentil soup + whole‑grain roll (25 g)

Day 6 – Breakfast: 2‑egg omelette + cheese (28 g)
Lunch: Leftover bolognese (35 g)
Snack: Protein‑rich smoothie (milk + yoghurt) (15 g)
Dinner: Grilled fish (if on sale) or extra chicken (30 g)

Day 7 – Breakfast: Oats + peanut butter + milk (20 g)
Lunch: Tuna & quinoa bowl (30 g)
Snack: Greek yoghurt (12 g)
Dinner: Soy mince tacos with lettuce and salsa (35 g)

sections.heading: 4. Smart Shopping & Prep Tips
sections.body: Saving money is as much about how you shop as what you buy. Follow these habits to stretch every dollar while keeping nutrition on point.
list: Buy in bulk when items are on sale – Pak'nSave’s “Buy One Get One Free” on frozen veg is a goldmine
Choose store‑brand products; they’re nutritionally identical to name brands at 30‑40 % less
Freeze portions of raw chicken or soy mince right after purchase to avoid waste
Cook a large batch of rice, lentils or oats on Sunday and portion into freezer‑safe bags
Use a kitchen scale to portion protein accurately – you’ll avoid over‑cooking and over‑spending

sections.heading: 5. Get More Value with Exercise NZ
sections.body: If you’re a member of Exercise NZ, you can access subsidised gym memberships (40‑70 % off) at participating clubs. That extra cash can be redirected into higher‑quality food or a small whey protein supplement if you need a convenient boost.
